boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNF spaces for studying, gathering, outdoor breaks, and hands-on campus involvement, supported by direct university sources.

cards.title: Thomas G. Carpenter Library
cards.subtitle: Building 12
cards.notes: Use the group-study rooms, public workstations, balcony seating, and research help to turn a solo work session into a shared project block.
cards.short_summary: A large campus library with reservable study rooms and research support.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies the Thomas G. Carpenter Library as Building 12 and says it provides group study rooms, public workstations, balcony seating, and research assistance.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's posted hours and reserve spaces through its website when needed.

cards.title: Library Group Collaboration Hubs
cards.subtitle: Thomas G. Carpenter Library, second floor
cards.notes: Reserve a hub when your group needs one shared screen for slides, web pages, or laptop work instead of crowding around a single device.
cards.short_summary: Second-floor library hubs with large interactive screens for group work.
cards.evidence_claim: The UNF Library says its Group Collaboration Hubs are on the second floor and let users wirelessly share a laptop screen for presentations, slides, videos, or web pages.
cards.access_notes: Reserve the hubs through the library's space-reservation link; confirm availability before arriving.

cards.title: John A. Delaney Student Union
cards.subtitle: Building 58, East and West
cards.notes: Use the Union as a practical meet-up point before an event, then browse its student-organization offices, activity programming, and dining areas.
cards.short_summary: The campus focal point for student activities, programs, dining, and organization offices.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF describes the John A. Delaney Student Union as the focal point for student activities and programs, dining facilities, and organizational offices.
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual office hours vary; check the Union or event calendar before planning a visit.

cards.title: Osprey Plaza
cards.subtitle: Between Student Union East and West
cards.notes: Meet beneath the partial cover between the Union buildings, then pause to look at the installed pavers and any scheduled tabling or vendor activity.
cards.short_summary: A partially covered Student Union gathering area used for varied event setups.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies Osprey Plaza as a partially covered open area between the East and West Student Union buildings that can host a variety of event types.
cards.source_title: Student Union Event Services Photo Gallery
cards.access_notes: The plaza is an event space; respect active setups and check campus programming for public activities.

cards.title: The Green
cards.subtitle: In front of the Fine Arts Center, Building 45
cards.notes: Walk through before or after class to see current student-organization tables, or use the lawn as a simple outdoor rendezvous near Fine Arts.
cards.short_summary: A high-traffic campus lawn in front of the Fine Arts Center.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF says The Green is in front of the Fine Arts Center, Building 45, and is a high-traffic campus location used for tabling.
cards.source_title: Student Union Event Services Photo Gallery
cards.access_notes: Tables and equipment are reservation-managed; open lawn use may be affected by scheduled events.

cards.entity_name: Frederick and Ophelia Tate Ogier Gardens
cards.title: Frederick and Ophelia Tate Ogier Gardens
cards.subtitle: North end of campus near Lot 18
cards.notes: Drop in during open hours to volunteer, ask for a garden task, or explore the beds and sitting areas; wear closed-toe shoes for volunteering.
cards.short_summary: A one-acre organic garden with volunteer work, workshops, and quiet seating.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF says Ogier Gardens has row crops, fruit trees, raised beds, sitting areas, volunteer opportunities, and no-appointment volunteer sign-in during open hours.
cards.source_title: Frederick and Ophelia Tate Ogier Gardens
cards.access_notes: Current posted garden hours are Tuesday 8–11 AM; Wednesday and Friday 8–11 AM and 4–8 PM.

cards.title: Goldenrod Trail
cards.subtitle: Robert W. Loftin Nature Trails
cards.notes: Take this longer loop when your group wants a walking break with varied habitats; stay on the marked route and bring water for the 2.85-mile distance.
cards.short_summary: A 2.85-mile UNF trail crossing several campus habitat types.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF describes Goldenrod Trail as a 2.85-mile trail through multiple habitats and says the nature trails are open daily from sunrise to sunset.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Follow posted trail rules; groups of 10 or more must register in advance.

cards.title: Blueberry Trail
cards.subtitle: Robert W. Loftin Nature Trails
cards.notes: Choose this 1.44-mile route for a shorter nature break around Lake Oneida, and use the permanent exercise stations only as intended.
cards.short_summary: A Lake Oneida loop with habitat views and permanent exercise stations.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF says Blueberry Trail is a 1.44-mile route around Lake Oneida that overlaps Goldenrod Trail in places and includes permanent exercise stations.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Follow posted trail rules; groups of 10 or more must register in advance.

cards.title: Gopher Tortoise Ridge
cards.subtitle: Robert W. Loftin Nature Trails
cards.notes: Use this short sandy route for a quick outdoor reset, keeping a respectful distance from wildlife and leaving animals and their burrows undisturbed.
cards.short_summary: A 0.78-mile sandy trail in a campus gopher tortoise habitat.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF identifies Gopher Tortoise Ridge as a 0.78-mile sandy trail with a healthy gopher tortoise population.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. UNF prohibits harassing wildlife or collecting plants and animals.

cards.title: Red Maple Boardwalk
cards.subtitle: Robert W. Loftin Nature Trails
cards.notes: Pick this accessible boardwalk for a slower shared walk through wetland habitat, stopping at the interpretive signs and sitting areas along the way.
cards.short_summary: An accessible 1,600-foot boardwalk through Buck Head Branch Swamp.
cards.evidence_claim: UNF says Red Maple Boardwalk is a 0.31-mile, wheelchair-accessible boardwalk through Buck Head Branch Swamp with sitting areas and interpretive signs.
cards.access_notes: Open daily from sunrise to sunset. Follow posted trail rules and remain on the boardwalk.
